title: ownerOrNotGriefed modifier has three edge-case bypasses: truncation-boundary, expired-window restart, and zero-rate vacuous pass

classification.assetImpact: Each bypass extends windowEnd by windowDuration without triggering the rate-floor defence. No direct asset theft; schedule-stretch is bounded per call and requires a specific state (truncation-equal rate, expired window with nonzero budget, or zero floor-truncated rate).
attackPath: Instance A (truncation boundary): requires newRate == rPre at truncated granularity while continuous-math rate is strictly lower; permissionless but narrow.
Instance B (expired-window restart): requires windowEnd already expired with residual budget; permissionless once that state exists.
Instance C (zero-rate vacuous pass): requires rewardBudget < windowDuration so rewardRate floors to 0; permissionless once that state exists.
classification.likelihood: low - each instance requires the pool to enter a specific degenerate state. Under normal funding these states are transient or avoidable.
classification.assumptions: Truncation coincidence, window expiry with residual budget, or dust-stranded budget (see F-08).
classification.externalRequirements: Owner leaves the pool in one of the degenerate states; primarily a defensive-coding concern.

justification: Low/QA. Defensive-completeness issue on the newly introduced ownerOrNotGriefed modifier. The primary protocol-function impact is already captured by F-01 (which shows the modifier is bypassed entirely via claim/stake/unstake). Once F-01's root cause is fixed (no unconditional window reset in _syncBudget), these edge cases become moot. Standalone, each instance requires a narrow degenerate state; effect is bounded per call and in all cases only rearranges the emission schedule rather than removing funds.
